correctness.rationale: For every p,q,r>0 and p>=r, convex-curve perimeter-halving lemma reduces dilation to half-perimeter H=s+t divided by shortest halving chord. Complete arclength symmetry reduction gives two affine-vector regimes; the stationary minimum h0 is feasible whenever it beats h1, because G-F=ps(p+r)(s-t)>=0. Hence delta=max{s/q,sqrt(q^2(s+t)^2+(pt+rs)^2)/(q(p+r))}, equivalently max{sec alpha, 2cos((alpha-beta)/2)/sin(alpha+beta)}. For alpha<=pi/4 second branch >=2; for alpha>pi/4 the beta-minimized branch is strictly decreasing while sec alpha is strictly increasing. Their unique crossing is in (pi/4,pi/3) with unique interior beta, yielding the displayed two equations and one similarity class. A separately written full-edge halving-chord optimizer matched formula in 2000 moderate-aspect random triples, maximum relative difference 5.40e-14, and stress-tested limiting aspect cases; 500 independent trig-formula tests agreed to 1.10e-15. Independent root solution alpha=1.0241728055456187, beta=0.3817722511939446, delta=1.9237956679610035. The finite checks are diagnostics only; the exact regime and monotonicity argument supplies the quantified proof.
residual_risks: Extremely ill-conditioned geometric shapes can cause floating-point cancellation in finite implementation; proof uses exact inequalities and does not rely on this numerical domain.
Global minimizer represented implicitly by two transcendental equations and a numerical root rather than an elementary closed form.

value.rationale: Geometric dilation is a natural worst-detour invariant in convex geometry and embedded networks. This theorem classifies a complete natural non-centrally-symmetric family of four-gons, identifies an exact two-mode shortest-halving-chord profile, and proves a uniquely asymmetric global optimizer strictly below the symmetric square/rhombus bound 2. The exact invariant and extremizer are not known from or immediately implied by published generic bounds; no broader arbitrary-quadrilateral result is claimed.
residual_risks: Value is a precise natural-family classification, not a general sharp bound for all convex quadrilaterals.
